correctness.rationale: For the closed nondegenerate circular cone the polar half-angle is β=π/2−α. On S³ the polar-angle density is (2/π)sin²θ, so the two cap integrals give v₀ and v₄ in the record. The published circular-cone interior formula gives v₁=cos²α/2, v₂=2sinαcosα/π, v₃=sin²α/2. These are positive and sum with the caps to 1. Substitution yields R(β),16/π²,R(α) for the three quotients. For R, x−sin x cos x is strictly positive by its derivative 2sin²x. The numerator of its log derivative with the stated positive denominator is x(1+2cos²x)−3sin x cos x. It vanishes at zero and its derivative is 4sin x(sin x−x cos x)>0 since sin x−x cos x=∫₀ˣu sin u du. Thus R strictly increases from 3π²/16 to infinity; 4/3<3π²/16<2 and 3/2<16/π²<9/4. Since β decreases with α, only k=1 crosses, with equality just at the unique interior threshold, and k=2 obstructs binomial ULC throughout. The excluded endpoints have changing support. The exact threshold and numerical values agree with independent 75-digit bisection on the cross-multiplied equation (/workspace/cone_replay.py): β≈0.5861771479686967924, α≈0.9846191788261998268 radians ≈56.41452337437811814°. This decimal check is not a root-uniqueness proof. The frozen checker was inspected, not run. Bibliographic clarification: ALMT arXiv v2 locates the interior formula in App. D.1, Eq. (D.2); the difference from the frozen locator is not a mathematical error.

value.rationale: In the very family used to disprove general Poisson ULC, a sharp classification answers which apertures still satisfy it, identifies the only failing index, and distinguishes the two normalizations. The exact boundary and equality case are meaningful benchmarks for questions about conic intrinsic volumes; value is not assigned merely to the numerical cutoff or to the easy central quotient.
